variants.stem: Both the test specimen and known external positive control lack signal. Which listed interpretation is appropriate?
variants.explanation: A failed positive control means the assay run has not demonstrated acceptable performance, so the test result is invalid.

variants.stem: A calcified specimen requires antigen detection and RNA localization. Which listed decalcification approach best protects both analytes?
variants.explanation: Validated EDTA chelation is generally preferred over strong acid when antigens and nucleic acids must be preserved.

variants.stem: After retrieval time is increased, tissue detaches and nonspecific staining rises. Which listed effect best describes excessive heat retrieval?
variants.explanation: Excessive heat or retrieval duration can damage morphology, detach sections, and increase background.

variants.stem: A housekeeping-gene probe is included with an RNA ISH assay. Which listed function does it serve?
variants.explanation: An ISH positive-control probe evaluates analyte preservation and whether the assay steps worked in the specimen.

variants.stem: Which listed endogenous activity must commonly be blocked or controlled in an HRP/DAB method?
variants.explanation: Endogenous peroxidase can react with HRP chromogen systems and create nonspecific DAB deposition.

variants.stem: A tyramide-amplified assay produces strong nonspecific signal. Which listed issue requires the closest attention?
variants.explanation: Tyramide improves sensitivity but also amplifies background when reagent specificity, blocking, or washing is inadequate.
